$comment: The Lost Letters in the Hall of Records (Q1.7, Pell): each letter is a captain's problem, filed in the cubby (bin) that fixes it, or back in the tray when it isn't a job for any bin (the decoy). A wrong filing hands it back with the bin's own description and the letter's `need`, or the letter's own `wrong` reason, cited. The bins are the course's Settings areas in the app's order (01 · Settings, "Settings reference: What each area controls"); the game shows them on the cabinets' name plates (the last on brown) and keys them 1-9, 0. `cites` are course sections (README anchor, its hash in lock.json, the section's name).

bins.name: General
bins.holds: **General** checks for app updates, sets where repositories are stored, and changes the theme.

bins.name: Accounts
bins.holds: **Accounts** shows your account information and adds another GitHub account.

bins.name: Sessions
bins.holds: **Sessions** manages sessions and chats, the response style, app-wide instructions and branch naming.

bins.name: Themes
bins.holds: **Themes** selects and customizes the app theme.

bins.name: Accessibility
bins.holds: **Accessibility** has display zoom, keyboard shortcuts, and notifications and announcements.

bins.name: Voice dictation
bins.holds: **Voice dictation** sets up the microphone, its shortcut and the transcription models.

bins.name: Customize
bins.holds: **Customize** points you to the **Customize** view in the sidebar, for MCP servers, plugins, skills and canvases.

bins.name: Model providers
bins.holds: **Model providers** connects models from other providers with your own API keys.

bins.name: Experimental
bins.holds: **Experimental** lets you try preview features that can change or be removed.

bins.name: Projects
bins.holds: **Projects** holds each project’s own settings, such as **Show in sidebar**, sandbox rules and the default branch.

items.text: I sail for two fleets now, and the second one gave me its own GitHub login. How do I get both into the app?
items.need: This captain needs a second GitHub sign-in in the app.

items.text: My eyes aren’t what they were. The words in the app are too small, and I’d like the whole thing bigger.
items.need: This captain needs the app bigger on the screen, so it’s easier to read.

themes.text: **Themes** changes how the app looks, not how big it is. Making everything bigger helps the captain read it.

items.text: Your agent’s answers run on for pages! I want short, plain replies from now on, whatever I’m working on.
items.need: This is about how the agent replies, every time you work with it.

items.text: My company pays for models from another provider. I want to use them in the app with our own API key.
items.need: Think about where you’d bring your own key for another provider’s models.

items.text: This bug’s a nasty one, across several files. I want a stronger model, and more thinking, for this one task.
items.need: No area in Settings picks the model for one task. Is this a Settings job at all?

providers.text: **Model providers** connects extra providers with your own keys. It doesn’t replace the model picker below the prompt box.

items.text: I connected a project I hardly use. I’d like it out of my sidebar, but I don’t want to lose it.
items.need: This is a setting for one project, not for the whole app.

items.text: I want to add an MCP server, so the agent can reach our ticket tracker. Where’s that kept?
items.need: An MCP server extends what the app can do.

text.trayWhy: There’s an area in Settings for this one. Look for the closest match.
text.sortRest: Sort the rest of Pell’s letters
text.filedTray: Back in Pell’s tray: not a Settings job.
text.noTalk: Talk to Pell to finish up in the Hall of Records.
text.hint1: Read the letter for what the captain’s trying to do, Captain. Then think where that lives in Settings.
text.hint2: I’ve marked the right spot for this letter. Open the bundle and look for the glow.
text.hint3: There, I’ve filed one for you. Keep going!
text.title: The Lost Letters
text.close: Step away from the desk (Esc). Your letters stay filed.
